name: Glycogen Storage Disease Due to Glycogen Synthase Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Glycogen Storage Disease Type 0

criteria.description: Fasting hypoglycemia with low or absent ketones and postprandial hyperglycemia
Demonstration of deficient glycogen synthase enzyme activity in liver biopsy or cultured fibroblasts
Identification of pathogenic variants in the GYS2 gene
Histological evidence of decreased glycogen storage in hepatocytes
Abnormal glucose and lactate response during fasting and feeding tests

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of fasting hypoglycemia with low ketones plus either deficient glycogen synthase enzyme activity or pathogenic GYS2 gene variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is increasingly preferred over invasive liver biopsy for confirmation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Fasting hypoglycemia with absent or low ketonemia
searchTerms: low blood sugar when fasting without ketones
low sugar and absent ketones during fasting

common.symptomName: Hepatomegaly due to altered glycogen storage
searchTerms: enlarged liver from abnormal sugar storage
liver swelling due to glycogen buildup
big liver caused by altered glycogen

common.symptomName: Growth retardation or failure to thrive

searchTerms: slightly high lactic acid after eating
seizures caused by low blood sugar
muscle weakness or low muscle tone
reduced muscle strength or floppy muscles

occasional.symptomName: Irritability or behavioral changes during hypoglycemia

laboratory: Fasting hypoglycemia with low or absent ketones
Elevated liver transaminases in some cases
imaging: Ultrasound showing hepatomegaly without structural abnormalities
genetic: Pathogenic variants in GYS2 gene confirmed by molecular genetic testing
other: Reduced glycogen content in liver biopsy
Decreased glycogen synthase enzyme activity in liver tissue or fibroblasts

distinguishingFeatures: Severe fasting hypoglycemia with lactic acidosis and hyperuricemia
Presence of hepatomegaly with glycogen accumulation
Episodes triggered by fructose ingestion or fasting

redFlags: Recurrent severe hypoglycemia unresponsive to standard feeding
Development of seizures or altered consciousness during fasting
references: Rake JP et al. Glycogen storage disease type 0: clinical, biochemical, and molecular genetic features. J Inherit Metab Dis. 2002;25(6): 485-494.
Chou JY et al. Glycogen storage diseases: diagnosis and treatment. Curr Opin Pediatr. 2010;22(6): 696-703.
Orphanet: Glycogen storage disease due to glycogen synthase deficiency (ORPHA:308520)
